title: Senior Sales Engineer (Paris, France)
Thermal Test and Modelling Engineer
description:
Ready to make connectivity from space universally accessible, secure and actionable? Then you’ve come to the right place!

E-Space is bridging Earth and space to enable hyper-scaled deployments of Internet of Things (IoT) solutions and services. We are building a highly-advanced low Earth orbit (LEO) space system that will fundamentally change the design, economics, manufacturing and service delivery associated with traditional satellite and terrestrial IoT systems.

We’re intentional, we’re unapologetically curious and we’re 100% committed to innovate space-based communications and deliver actionable intelligence that will expand global economies, protect space and our planet and enhance our overall quality of life.


What is the role: 

We are seeking a Thermal Engineer to own the thermal analysis and testing of our space products, such as sensors and actuators. The role centers on building thermal models and correlating them with test data, and on planning and running thermal test campaigns in house. It is a hands-on position: you will instrument and run tests yourself and use the results to improve both the design and our test infrastructure. This position is based in our Toulouse office. 


What you will do:

  • Develop and maintain thermal models (analytical and numerical) of units such as sensors and actuators, from early design trades to flight predictions. 

  • Perform thermal analyses (steady-state, transient, worst-case hot and cold) to support design reviews and recommend design changes. 

  • Define thermal test campaigns: test plans, predictions, temperature profiles, instrumentation, and pass/fail criteria from requirements and qualification margins. 

  • Operate our in-house thermal test facility: run thermal cycling tests, coordinate thermal vacuum (TVAC) campaigns, and own the test reports. 

  • Correlate models with test data to refine predictions and margins and feed the results back into the design. 

  • Improve our test infrastructure: identify capability gaps, specify and procure equipment, design fixtures and thermal interfaces, and commission new setups. 

  • Act as the thermal point of contact for our units toward the spacecraft team: unit thermal budgets, interface boundary conditions, and unit models for the spacecraft thermal model. 

  • Support spacecraft Assembly, Integration, and Test (AIT) through system-level thermal balance testing.


    • What you bring to this role:

  • BS + 8 years / MS + 5 years in Mechanical, Aerospace, or Thermal Engineering, or equivalent, with professional experience in thermal engineering of space or electronic hardware. 

  • Solid grounding in space heat transfer: radiation in vacuum, conduction and contact conductance across bolted interfaces, and multi-layer insulation (MLI). 

  • Hands-on experience building thermal models with standard thermal analysis tools, running worst-case analyses, and correlating models with test data. 

  • Hands-on experience planning and running thermal tests (thermal cycling or TVAC) on space or electronic hardware, from test plan to test report. 

  • Ability to instrument a test article: thermocouple selection and bonding, heater sizing and placement, thermal interface materials, and data acquisition and real-time monitoring, with ESD-safe, clean handling of sensitive hardware. 

  • Excellent teamwork, communication, and documentation skills, with professional proficiency in English; comfortable in a hands-on, fast-paced startup environment.


    • Bonus points:

  • Experience with Python to post-process test data and automate model correlation. 

  • Experience designing or specifying thermal test equipment such as TVAC chambers, thermal plates, or shrouds. 

  • Knowledge of spacecraft thermal control hardware: heat pipes, radiators, coatings, and heater circuits. 

  • Experience using AI/LLM tools to accelerate development, analysis, and documentation, with sound judgment about their limits.

title: Database Engineer (Stateful Services)
description:
Build the infrastructure behind the next generation of AI-powered customer communications.

Diabolocom is building an AI-first communication platform where AI and human agents, business workflows and communication channels work together seamlessly.
As we enter our next phase of growth, we are looking for a Database Engineer (Stateful Services) to help build and operate the infrastructure foundation behind the platform.
This is a unique opportunity to work on an infrastructure environment combining carrier-grade voice systems, on-premise data centers, distributed systems and AI workloads, while helping us build the reliability and operational maturity required to support 3x growth.
You will report to the newly forming Stateful Services Lead and work closely with Engineering, SRE and Infrastructure teams to improve the reliability, scalability and evolution of our stateful systems.

Your mission

Your goal is to build, operate and improve Diabolocom’s stateful services, with a strong focus on databases and data stores.
You will help ensure that our databases and stateful systems remain highly available, reliable and performant, while evolving our infrastructure so that maintenance, upgrades and scaling can be performed safely and with minimal to no downtime.
Working closely with the Stateful Services Lead, you will take ownership of specific technical projects and contribute to the evolution of our stateful infrastructure.

You will:

  • Operate and maintain our stateful services, including PostgreSQL, ClickHouse, Redis, RabbitMQ and Kafka/Redpanda.
  • Contribute to the design, evolution and scaling of our database infrastructure, with 50+ PostgreSQL clusters and increasingly complex data workloads.
  • Work on projects aimed at making database maintenance, upgrades and migrations safer and less disruptive to our services.
  • Improve high availability, replication, failover, backup/restore and disaster recovery across our stateful systems.
  • Contribute to rebuilding our PostgreSQL clusters to support automatic failover between data centers and reduce the impact of maintenance operations.
  • Help improving our queueing infrastructure, including projects such as quorum-based RabbitMQ.
  • Help building and maintaining stable Redis infrastructure and improve the reliability of our stateful services.
  • Investigate and solve complex performance, scalability and reliability issues across databases and distributed systems.
  • Work closely with development teams to understand their needs, support their use of databases and help them build reliable solutions.
  • Collaborate with SRE, networking and infrastructure teams to ensure that our stateful services operate reliably within our broader infrastructure.
  • Contribute to monitoring, automation and operational practices that make our infrastructure easier and safer to operate.
  • Participate in our on-call and incident management rotation, helping diagnose and resolve production issues when needed.
  • Stay hands-on and close to the technology: you will be expected to understand how our systems work, how they fail and how to improve them.

Who we are looking for

We’re looking for a technically strong and hands-on Database Engineer who enjoys solving complex infrastructure problems and taking ownership of production systems where reliability really matters.
You have experience operating databases or stateful services in production and understand that running these systems is about much more than simply maintaining them. You know how to troubleshoot them, how they behave under load, how they fail, and how to make them more reliable as they scale.
You’ll work on specific technical projects defined with the Stateful Services Lead, while having the autonomy to investigate problems, propose solutions and contribute to technical decisions.
We care more about your technical depth, curiosity and ability to take ownership than the exact number of years of experience you have.

Must Have

  • Strong hands-on experience as a DBA, Database Engineer, SRE or similar, with solid experience in PostgreSQL.
  • Experience operating and maintaining production databases, including upgrades, migrations, replication, backups, recovery, monitoring and performance troubleshooting.
  • Good understanding of high availability and reliability for stateful systems: failover, redundancy, replication, disaster recovery and minimising downtime during maintenance.
  • Good understanding of distributed systems, including replication, consistency, fault tolerance and the challenges of operating stateful services at scale.
  • Experience working with on-premise infrastructure or a willingness and ability to quickly adapt to an on-premise/bare-metal environment.
  • Good system design skills and the ability to reason about scalability, reliability and performance.
  • Experience collaborating closely with software development teams, understanding their requirements and helping them build reliable solutions around databases and stateful services.
  • Strong troubleshooting and problem-solving skills, with the ability to investigate complex production issues.
  • Strong hands-on mindset: you enjoy getting into the technical details and solving problems yourself.
  • Comfortable participating in on-call and incident management.
  • Fluent English, both written and spoken. French or other languages are a plus.

Nice to Have

Experience with some of the following:
  • ClickHouse or another complex database/data platform.
  • Kafka or Redpanda and event-streaming infrastructure.
  • RabbitMQ, particularly quorum-based configurations.
  • Redis and distributed caching.
  • Other database technologies such as Elasticsearch/OpenSearch, MySQL, Cassandra or MongoDB.
  • Advanced Linux systems administration, including processes, storage, networking and troubleshooting.
  • Bare-metal infrastructure and data-center environments.
  • Observability and monitoring of stateful systems.
  • Capacity planning, performance analysis and load testing.
  • Infrastructure automation and configuration management.
  • Incident management, root-cause analysis and post-mortem practices.

About You

  • You take ownership. When you see a reliability or scalability problem, you investigate it and work towards a solution.
  • You are genuinely technical. You like understanding how things work under the hood and are comfortable diving deep when something breaks.
  • You think in systems. You understand that databases don't operate in isolation and enjoy working across infrastructure, networking, SRE and development teams.
  • You care about reliability. You want systems that can be maintained, upgraded and scaled without putting the business at risk.
  • You are pragmatic. You can make sensible technical trade-offs in complex environments.
  • You are curious and self-driven. You learn by doing, investigate unfamiliar technologies and are comfortable figuring things out independently.
  • You enjoy solving complex problems. You like working on systems where there isn't always an obvious answer.
  • You communicate clearly. You can explain technical topics and work effectively with the teams relying on your services.
  • You are comfortable taking responsibility. You don't need to be a manager to have an impact or take the lead on a technical problem.

Why join us

  • Own critical infrastructure: your work will directly impact the reliability and scalability of Diabolocom’s platform.
  • Solve complex technical challenges: work with large-scale databases and stateful services, including PostgreSQL, ClickHouse, Kafka, Redis and RabbitMQ.
  • Work on real infrastructure challenges: help improve PostgreSQL clusters, cross-data-center failover, RabbitMQ and Redis reliability.
  • Stay hands-on: spend your time solving challenging technical problems rather than managing people.
  • Learn and grow: work across databases, distributed systems, messaging and infrastructure in a diverse technical environment.
  • Work across teams: collaborate closely with Engineering, SRE and Infrastructure to build reliable systems at scale.

Recruitment Process

  1. Introductory call with Talent Acquisition (1h)
  2. Interview with Sergey, our CTO (1h)
  3. On-site System Design interview with Sergey (1h)
    Work through a technical case study and explore your system design approach.
  4. Cultural fit interview with the Team (1h)

Logistics

🏢 Hybrid model: 3 days onsite / 2 days remote
💻 Equipment: choose your preferred setup (Mac/Linux + monitors)
🍽  Lunch vouchers
🚇 Navigo: 50% of the monthly pass reimbursed

One More Thing

We are not necessarily looking for someone who has already worked in this exact role or with every technology in our stack.
The strongest candidates are often engineers who have built and operated complex infrastructure, taken ownership of production systems and learned new technologies along the way.
If you enjoy solving difficult technical problems, want to work close to the infrastructure and are excited by the challenge of making stateful systems more reliable and scalable — we would love to talk.

title: Chief Financial Officer
description:
Most CFOs inherit a finance function.

This one gets to build it.

quinn is an app-based, managed payroll and employment-administration service. We run it for private households employing a cleaner, nanny, or caretaker, and for businesses that manage employment relationships at scale. The customer stays the legal employer — quinn registers the employment, runs payroll, and handles social insurance, taxes, and filings on their behalf, automated end to end.

Where everyone else sells software, quinn sells the outcome. We hold the power of attorney for every customer, take decisions, do the work, and take legal responsibility for the result.

The purpose behind it is simple: Fair employment. For all. That means making correct and fair employment simple and accessible for any employer and any employee, in any market quinn enters.

Where we stand

Thousands of clients rely on us. Last year alone, over CHF 200 million ran through our platform. We are at CHF 7 million ARR and growing. The Swiss business is profitable. We have acquired two new businesses in the last twelve months. A hungry team of over 50 people (and 5 dogs) in offices in Switzerland, Germany and the United Kingdom. And we are raising our next round.

We do not have a finance function yet. We have an external accountant, a signed audit, and a CEO and COO who know exactly what they need to run this company — but cannot build it alone.

That is the opening.

Tasks

What you will own

Everything financial:

  • Banking architecture across multiple currencies, countries, and entities. Monthly close that actually closes on time.
  • Compliance in multiple jurisdictions via external partners you recruit and manage.
  • The financial diligence in our roll-up strategy when we acquire — and the structuring of acquisition financing when deals need to be funded.
  • A financial model that investors love to look at. The data room when we raise.

You will report to David (CEO) and work closely with Lad (COO), who owns the P&L and will be your closest counterpart on the operational side. You will present to the board. You will be in the room for every capital allocation decision.

There is no team. There is no process to maintain. There is a blank sheet and a business that is ready to run properly.

The first year

Your first year at quinn is one of the rare opportunities where you get to make every decision that matters. Which tools. Which banks. Which partners. How we report, how we model, how we show up to investors. All of it is yours to design.

You will spend the first months getting under the hood — taking over the books, understanding the gaps, and fixing what needs fixing first. You will build the reporting infrastructure that gives leadership real visibility to steer the company across every product and revenue stream.

You will analyze the first potential merger and acquisition targets and sit in rooms where the financial direction of the company gets decided, and you will be the person with the numbers.

By the end of the year, you will have built something real: a finance function that works, a roll-up strategy that has financial legs, and a leadership team that trusts you completely. Most people at this level spend years waiting for that kind of ownership. Here it happens within months.

Requirements

Who we are looking for

You have been CFO or Head of Finance at a scale-up — a SaaS, marketplace, or tech-enabled services company. You have worked across more than one international market. You are comfortable closing the books yourself, not just reviewing what others produce. You have built financial infrastructure before — not inherited it.

You are equally at home in B2C and B2B — and you understand what it means to manage the unit economics, reporting, and compliance obligations for both within a single business.

You think in MRR, ARR, NRR, CAC payback, and LTV:CAC ratio. You have worked with investors. You understand what a roll-up strategy looks like financially, and you have the accounting basics to back it up. You know the difference between managing a finance function and doing the finance — and you are built for the latter.

Most importantly: You want this. Not a senior finance role at a large company. This one. The blank sheet, the multiple markets, the acquisitions to integrate, the round to prepare, the opportunity. The kind of thing you only get to do once.

The Team

We are a small, fast, direct team. We do not have a lot of process, a lot of hierarchy, or a lot of patience for people who need it. We do have a profitable core business, a clear strategy, an ambitious plan, and five values we actually mean: Be open, Own it, Speak up, Keep it simple, Bias for action

The CFO is one of the most important hires we will make this year. We are not rushing it and we are not filling a seat. We are looking for the person who looks at this and thinks: Finally!

description:
Our Mission

At Laelaps AI, we believe robotics is entering a transformative decade, much like the arrival of the internet. Advances in AI, cloud computing, and hardware are reshaping what autonomous systems can do. Our mission is to build the intelligent software that powers physical security in the real world - enabling robots and sensors to handle dangerous and critical tasks that humans shouldn't have to. By engineering the orchestration layer for intelligent security, we aim to create a world that is safer, more secure, and more resilient.

We're a strong founding team based in Zurich, backed by visionary investors and advisors. We are engineering the future of security today!

The Role

You will own the research question at the centre of LEA, our foundation model of the physical world: can a model learn what normally happens on a site, by place, hour and weather, so that an anomaly is simply what it did not expect? The first version is a probabilistic memory of each site. The next is a world model across every site that predicts the next state in latent space, starting from open world-model weights and growing on field data nobody else holds.

Our robots and cameras run on live security sites around the clock, and every event is kept with its clip, the model's verdict and the operator's outcome. That record is your dataset. You will work alongside our perception and model engineers, and your results go into production, not only into papers.

What You'll Work On

  • Site memory: a learned, probabilistic model of each site: which people, vehicles and robots are where, at what hour, in what weather, and how the scene usually unfolds.

  • Anomaly as surprise: replace rule-based alerting with measured surprise, and work out how to evaluate it when real incidents are rare.

  • World model: post-train open world-model weights on aligned multi-sensor field sequences, JEPA-style, predicting in latent space rather than pixels.

  • Transfer: from one site's memory to a model of all of them, and representations that carry across sites and domains.

  • Research direction: choose the questions, design the experiments, and decide what is true before it ships.

Who We're Looking For

A research scientist who has led work on world models, self-supervised learning or probabilistic spatio-temporal modelling, and who wants to see it run on real sites. You are rigorous about what a result does and does not show, and pragmatic about getting it into a product.

Your Background

  • PhD in machine learning, computer vision, robotics or a related field, with first-author publications at top venues.

  • Research experience in world models, video or latent prediction, self-supervised representation learning, or probabilistic modelling of spatio-temporal data.

  • Experience with anomaly or novelty detection where positives are rare.

  • Strong PyTorch and the engineering to run your own experiments at scale.

Nice to Have

  • Scene graphs, multi-object tracking or trajectory forecasting.

  • Bayesian or probabilistic deep learning.

title: Software Engineer, Robot Autonomy (Reliability & Test Infrastructure)
description:
Our Mission

At Laelaps AI, we believe robotics is entering a transformative decade, much like the arrival of the internet. Advances in AI, cloud computing, and hardware are reshaping what autonomous systems can do. Our mission is to build the intelligent software that powers physical security in the real world - enabling robots and sensors to handle dangerous and critical tasks that humans shouldn't have to. By engineering the orchestration layer for intelligent security, we aim to create a world that is safer, more secure, and more resilient.

We're a strong founding team based in Zurich, backed by visionary investors and advisors. We are engineering the future of security today!

The Role

You will own the path a code change takes from commit to robot, and the evidence behind every gate on that path. Today the honest answer to "is this build safe?" is "it worked on the test robot." You will replace that with a system: the simulation environment the team tests against, the regression suites that run on every change, the hardware-in-the-loop rigs, and the release gates that decide whether a build can go onto a robot that will patrol a customer site alone tonight.

This is the first engineer dedicated to reliability and test infrastructure, and it sits in our Robot Autonomy team, next to the engineers building perception, localisation, planning and locomotion. Our robots patrol security sites, critical infrastructure and defence facilities without a human present, so a bad release is not a rollback: it is a customer incident. Within six months, nothing should reach a customer robot without passing something you built.

What You'll Work On

  • Release pipeline: code change, automated tests, simulation at scale, staging robot, pilot site, full rollout, with explicit pass criteria at every gate and nothing advancing without meeting them.

  • Simulation as infrastructure: a GPU-backed simulation environment (Isaac Sim today) running continuously, so engineers test against scenarios instead of queueing for the one robot in the lab.

  • Scenario libraries and regression suites: coverage across the whole on-robot stack, perception through locomotion, and the infrastructure to run thousands of scenarios on every change.

  • Hardware-in-the-loop: bench rigs and test procedures on the physical robots for what simulation cannot tell you.

  • Failure injection: drop sensors, degrade LiDAR returns, kill the network link, corrupt odometry, then verify the system degrades and recovers the way we tell customers it does.

  • Field incidents to tests: when a robot misbehaves on site, reproduce it deterministically and turn it into a permanent regression test.

  • Reproducibility: log capture, replay tooling, deterministic seeds, versioned scenarios, and coverage metrics that are honest about what they do not cover.

  • Acceptance criteria: turn product and customer requirements into measurable tests, and report against them without softening the numbers.

Who We're Looking For

A test, validation or reliability engineer who has shipped a product where failure had consequences, and who has seen what changes when a fleet goes from one unit to fifty. You treat simulation and CI as production infrastructure that you own, not tools you consume. You have judgment about what is worth testing: we want a safety net, not a wall of green ticks that hides the real risk. And you are comfortable being the person who says a build is not going out.

Your Background

  • 4+ years in test, validation, reliability, SRE or platform engineering on a product that shipped to customers.

  • Experience with a complex system at scale: autonomous driving, drones, industrial automation, medical devices or similar.

  • Strong Python and/or C++, with solid CI/CD and containerised infrastructure skills.

  • Hands-on with a robotics simulator run as production infrastructure: Isaac Sim preferred, Gazebo, MuJoCo or equivalent accepted.

  • Comfortable owning cloud infrastructure and GPU orchestration, not just consuming it.

  • Enough hardware literacy to read a timing problem or a flaky sensor trace, and the judgment to know when to hand it to Hardware.

Nice to Have

  • Fleet telemetry and observability (Grafana, Prometheus, OpenTelemetry).

  • On-prem, air-gapped or defence deployment experience.

wo-afstudeerstage, vanaf februari 2027

Dit is jouw uitdaging

Iedere maand vragen we tussen de 6000 en 7500 bedrijven in Nederland naar hun verwachtingen voor de omzet van hun bedrijf. Bij elkaar verzameld en gemiddeld blijkt dit een goede voorspelling voor de omzetontwikkeling van bedrijfstakken.   • Het publiceren van ondersteunende informatie voor gebruikers van onze enquête om deze beter te kunnen interpreteren en gebruiken voor voorspellingen.

  • Het gebruiken van deze informatie om 'verdachte opgaven' in enquêtes later in het proces te ontdekken.

Een eerder (kort) onderzoek leverde verwarrende resultaten op waarbij de verbanden tussen verwachting en omzet niet duidelijk te zien waren. Vervolgens ga je op zoek naar antwoorden op de volgende vragen:

  • Hoe kunnen we deze data zo beschikbaar maken dat externe onderzoekers hier optimaal nut uit kunnen halen?

  • Wat vinden belanghebbende op dit gebied hiervan?

  • Hoe kunnen we intern deze verbanden inzetten om verdachte opgaven in andere enquêtes en bronnen te detecteren?

Het team Bedrijvenconjunctuur & Coördinatie bestaat uit ongeveer 25 medewerkers. Variërend van zeer ervaren medewerkers tot jonge mensen die nog aan het begin van hun loopbaan staan. Dit breng jij mee

Je volgt een wetenschappelijke opleiding met als studierichting economie, bedrijfseconomie, statistiek of dataverwerking.

Je hebt kennis van en wellicht ervaring met:

  • Statistiek;

  • Python en/of R;

  • Bedrijfseconomische begrippen zoals omzet, bedrijfsgrootte, rechtvorm en indexcijfers.

Je bent een enthousiaste en proactieve student die flexibel inspeelt op verschillende situaties. Je bent sociaal, weet tactvol te handelen en werkt graag samen met anderen om tot een goed resultaat te komen.

Omdat tijdens de stage alle communicatie – zowel mondeling als schriftelijk – in het Nederlands plaatsvindt, is een goede beheersing van de Nederlandse taal noodzakelijk.

  • leert om begrijpelijk te programmeren in R/Python;

title: Master Data Engineer
description:
About Vitestro

Founded in 2017 in Utrecht, Vitestro is pioneering the future of blood collection with the Aletta® Autonomous Robotic Phlebotomy Device™ (ARPD™). This groundbreaking medical device combines advanced multi-modal imaging (near-infrared, ultrasound, and Doppler ultrasound) with robotics and AI to perform the entire diagnostic blood draw procedure autonomously.

 

By addressing critical healthcare staffing shortages and improving patient experience, Vitestro is transforming one of the most common and essential medical procedures. With more than 130 team members and growing rapidly, we are scaling our impact. As we placed our first devices with customers, we are now expanding our team to ensure successful implementation and long-term reliability.

 

At Vitestro, we are committed to continuous innovation and improvement.

Master Data Engineer

As our Master Data Engineer, you own the accuracy and integrity of the master data behind every Aletta we build: items, bills of materials (BOMs), revisions and routings in our ERP system. You translate the engineering BOM released by R&D into the manufacturing BOM for products, sub-assemblies and spare parts. You also own the change control process between Engineering, Operations and Supply Chain, from the first change request to the verified change in the build. This is a newly created role in our Operations team.

First months at Vitestro

In your first months, your focus will be on two things. First, you set up the change process end to end: from an engineering change to its implementation in the build, including the impact on time and cost. You register changes, organize the impact assessment with Operations, Supply Chain and Quality, chair the change review board, and define effectivity and the disposition of existing stock. Second, you build the manufacturing BOMs for our products from the engineering BOMs. You structure sub-assemblies to match the assembly sequence, add consumables, packaging, labels, kitting and the make/buy split, and set up spare-part and service BOMs together with Service. Along the way, you define how system and module upgrades are managed through the BOM.

You become the single point of contact for master data and change implementation. You make sure every build uses the correct released configuration, so that each Device History Record traces back to the Device Master Record.

This is what success looks like:

After 12 months, engineering changes run through one controlled process, and every change is implemented, verified in the first build and closed in the change record. Product and spare-part BOMs are free of errors, and master data is audit-ready under ISO 13485. Engineering, Operations and Supply Chain know where a change stands and when it reaches the build. Regular comparisons between E-BOM, M-BOM and as-built show no open discrepancies.

You thrive at the intersection of engineering and operations. You are precise and process-minded, you keep the discipline when others are in a hurry, and you are comfortable holding a change that isn't ready yet.


What You’ll Bring:

  • A bachelor's or master's background in Mechanical, Mechatronics or Industrial Engineering, or a similar technical field

  • 3+ years in master data, BOM, configuration or engineering change management in a manufacturing environment, preferably MedTech or high-tech

  • Experience with an ERP system, such as Odoo, SAP or Exact

  • Solid understanding of E-BOM and M-BOM structures, item lifecycle and revision control

  • Strong ability to align cross-functional stakeholders and keep process discipline

  • Comfortable working with detail: analytical, accurate and process-minded

  • Excellent communication skills

  • Fluent in English

Nice to have:

  • Experience in a regulated environment (ISO 13485, DMR/DHR, design transfer)

  • Familiarity with a PLM system

  • Experience reading technical drawings, and basic 3D CAD knowledge

  • Experience with advanced Excel or data tooling for data validation

  • Dutch language skills

How We Work

At Vitestro, ownership is not a slogan - it is an expectation. We trust people to take responsibility, make decisions, and drive work forward.

We believe breakthroughs happen when talented people combine dedication, accountability, and teamwork. That means:

  • We take initiative rather than wait for direction.

  • We focus on execution and delivering results.

  • We proactively remove blockers and help each other succeed.

  • We challenge ideas, not people.

  • We continuously learn, improve, and raise the bar.

  • We celebrate team success over individual heroics.

We move fast, but we do so thoughtfully. We care deeply about quality because the technology we build ultimately impacts patients and healthcare professionals.

If you are looking for an environment where you can make a significant contribution, take ownership of meaningful work, and be surrounded by highly motivated colleagues, we'd love to meet you.

What we offer 

  • Competitive salary including pension plan 

  • 25 days of annual leave based on a full-time position 

  • Hybrid work model 

  • Working together in a high-skilled team with our home base in Utrecht 

  • Frequent out-of-work activities with our team, and annual company weekend away.

  • Training budget 

  • Opportunity to be key shaper of a new global industry niche: autonomous medical robotics 

We’re big fans of working from the office – this is where team spirit comes alive. At the same time, we offer flexibility, allowing up to two (out of 5) days of working from home for those who prefer it. 

Are you excited? 

We totally understand that and so are we! By joining us, you can play an active role in changing the future of health care. Excited to join our revolution? Then we’d love to hear from you! 

If you think you've got what it takes, but you don't meet all the requirements - we still recommend you apply. We would love to learn about your interest and experience and consider if you can be a good fit for Vitestro. Nobody is a perfect fit, and we welcome applications with imperfections. We offer a learning environment where we grow together!

Voor onze afdeling Controls Engineering in Gorinchem zijn we per direct op zoek naar een ervaren Senior Controls Engineer voor het programmeren van de aansturing van onze nieuwste voedselproductie lijnen voor onze klanten van het merk Tromp uit Gorinchem. Dit betreft een full time functie, met veel afwisseling en hulp van betrokken teamgenoten om de meest slimme/ efficiënte besturingsoplossingen te bouwen.

Ontwerp en programmeer jij graag de nieuwste deegverwerkingsmachines van AMF Bakery Systems? Step dan in als Senior Controls Engineer! Heb je ervaring als software, controls of mechatronica engineer in machinebouw, ben je vertrouwd met programmeren in structured text en ben je bekend met Siemens besturingstechniek? Hecht je aan betrokken en slimme collega's waarmee je samen 'state of the art' voedselproductielijnen ontwerpt, programmeert en bouwt? Super, dan zijn we op zoek naar jou!

Wat bieden wij jou?

  • Maandsalaris tussen €4.00,00 en €5.800,00 o.b.v. 40 uur; afhankelijk van jouw kennis en ervaring, excl. toeslagen

  • Reiskostenvergoeding (€0,25 / km); vitaliteitsbudget tot €25,00 netto per maand en een zeer goede pensioenvoorziening (PME)

  • Flexibele werktijden, deels thuiswerken mogelijk

  • Vakantiegeld 8%

  • CAO Metalektro waaronder 27 vakantiedagen en 13 adv dagen per jaar

  • Winstdeling, afhankelijk van de winst betreffende het jaar, tot max. €2.000,00

  • Uitstekende opleidingsmogelijkheden zodat jouw vakkennis up to date is en blijft

  • Werken in een enthousiast en innoverend team

  • Informele werksfeer, teamuitjes, vrijdagmiddagborrel

  • Alle ruimte om te groeien in je functie afhankelijk van jouw ambities


Wat ga je doen:

  • Ontwikkelen / programmeren, configureren en integreren van software van onze machines (PLC + HMI). We passen veel techniek toe van Siemens en Allen Bradley.

  • Testen op locatie Gorinchem (IO, netwerk, drives, functioneel)

  • Softwarematig helpen met voorbereiden van productielijnen voor de FAT

  • Inzetten van jouw software expertise voor ondersteuning van Assembly, Buitendienst en aan klanten bij complexe software gerelateerde issues

  • Incidenteel naar de klant voor ondersteuning van commissioning van nieuwe productie lijnen

  • Als onze software expert werk je intensief samen met Electrical en Mechanical engineers, collega's van Sales, Projectmanagers, Assembly Engineers etc. Je bent dan vraagbaak en neemt besluiten mbt onze software oplossingen.

  • Bijdragen aan het continue verder verbeteren van onze technische controls oplossingen conform onze Markel Business aanpak

  • Helpen met verder standaardiseren van onze software oplossingen van onze product portfolio van het merk Tromp in Gorinchem.

  • Je werkt zelfstandig aan jouw projecten


  • HBO Elektrotechniek, Mechatronica of vergelijkbaar, of ROC Mechatronica niv 4 met ruime ervaring

  • Gedegen kennis van en ervaring met Siemens Tia Portal en of Allen Bradley Studio 5000

  • Kennis van hogere programmeertalen (vb. Structured text of VBA)

  • Teamplayer, pragmatisch en leergierig

  • Communicatief vaardig (goede beheersing van de Nederlandse en Engelse taal)

In wat voor bedrijf kom jij te werken?

Bij AMF Bakery Systems ben je onderdeel van een hechte en trotse groep collega’s die wereldwijd bijdraagt aan het succes van industriële bakkerijen. Wat ons verbindt, is onze drive om te innoveren én onze zorg voor de wereld om ons heen. Zo ontwikkelden wij samen de eerste industriële oven op waterstof – een grote stap richting een duurzamere toekomst.

We werken met ruim 220 collega’s in Nederland – vanuit Gorinchem, Amersfoort en Nieuwleusen – en maken deel uit van de internationale Markel Food Group. Binnen AMF voelt iedereen zich thuis: of je nu op kantoor werkt, in de werkplaats of bij de klant op locatie. We geloven dat we samen sterker zijn als iedereen zich welkom, gehoord en gewaardeerd voelt.

Diversiteit en inclusie zitten dan ook in ons DNA. We staan open voor mensen met verschillende achtergronden en ideeën, omdat we weten dat juist die mix leidt tot slimme oplossingen en sterke teams. Jij hoort erbij – precies zoals je bent.

Samen bouwen we aan iets groters dan alleen machines. We bouwen aan een toekomst waarin we samen kunnen groeien, leren en impact maken.

title: Senior Projectmanager
description:
Jouw Missie bij CCS

Geen dag is hetzelfde in deze rol. Samen met je collega’s zorg je ervoor dat wij succesvol onze softwareoplossingen bij klanten implementeren en dat onze klanten een excellente dienstverlening krijgen! Voor deze complexe systeemimplementaties en integratieprojecten zoeken we een zeer ervaren projectmanager. Je leert de verzekeringsbranche kennen en klanten helpen. Dat doe je niet alleen: je werkt samen met enthousiaste collega’s in een projectteam.

Voordelen voor de sollicitant

Als projectmanager krijg je veel verantwoordelijkheid, help je klanten en samen met je projectteam zet je mooie resultaten neer. Je kunt deels thuiswerken, deels op ons kantoor in Woerden en bij verschillende klanten in Nederland. Tijdelijk werken vanuit het buitenland kan ook dankzij onze workation-regeling (maximaal 30 dagen aaneengesloten per jaar).

Bij ons draait het om klantgericht werken én werkplezier. Daarom is er volop ruimte voor ontspanning en plezier. Denk aan een levend tafelvoetbaltoernooi, pubquiz en een bier- & wijnproeverij. Ons actieve Fun-team zorgt elke maand weer voor iets leuks.

En als je reislust nog niet is gestild met 25 vakantiedagen en een workation, dan kun je zelfs tot 20 extra verlofdagen bijkopen. Genoeg redenen om verder te lezen en te ontdekken of deze functie iets voor jou is, toch?


Een voorbeeld van je werkdag

Opstarten: Aan het begin van je werkdag heb je een dagstart met zowel collega’s als projectteamleden van de klant. Hierin bespreken jullie de voortgang, resultaten en eventuele hulpvragen.

Na de dagstart: Allereerst neem je nog wat tijd met een van de consultants naar aanleiding van de dagstart. Je coacht en begeleidt de consultant en helpt deze met een hulpvraag. Vervolgens ga je aan de slag met het opstellen van de voortgangsrapportage. Hiermee zorg je voor proactieve en transparante rapportage over het project aan de klant. De stuurgroep met de klant is volgende week, vandaag spreek je samen met de delivery manager deze stuurgroep voor. Wat zijn de belangrijkste punten voor de klant en voor CCS en hoe vliegen we die aan.

Na de lunch: Je checkt nog een paar tickets qua voortgang op het planboard, waarbij je de samenhang met de planning checkt. Vervolgens ga je naar de werksessie met het CCS projectmanagement guild. Hier werken jullie aan tickets om de CCS Prince2Agile projectmethodiek verder te verbeteren. Hierna heb je nog een afspraak met je collega van sales voor afstemming over een mogelijk vervolgproject bij de klant.

Wie jij bent

De ideale kandidaat beschikt over daadkracht, doorzettingsvermogen, enthousiasme en drive om projecten succesvol te leiden en verbeteringen door te voeren om te komen tot nog efficiëntere en klantgerichte projecten. Jij herkent jezelf in de volgende punten:

· Je wordt blij van projectmanagement en blijft kalm bij verschuivende prioriteiten;

· Je hebt bewezen ervaring met het succesvol uitvoeren van productsoftware-implementaties in een complexe, maar klantgerichte omgeving, binnen budget, planning en scope;

· Je hebt ruime ervaring met diverse projectmanagement en delivery methodieken, bij voorkeur een Prince2-, Ipma of PMI of Agile / scrum certificaat;

· Je vindt, net als wij, klanttevredenheid het uitgangspunt. Daarbij ben je in staat om de klantverwachtingen helder te analyseren, te managen en actief bij te sturen waar nodig;

· Je beheerst de Nederlandse en Engelse taal uitstekend in woord en geschrift;

· Jouw persoonlijkheid kenmerkt zich door: gestructureerd, motiverend, communicatief sterk, duidelijk, open, tikje eigenwijs, enthousiast, relativerend, creatief en pragmatisch;

· Je haalt energie uit het opstellen en bewaken van planningen, analyseren van gegevens en opstellen van duidelijke, gestructureerde rapportages en presentaties;

· Je hebt minimaal een afgeronde bachelor, bij voorkeur richting bedrijfskunde, bedrijfseconomie en/of informatica.

Wat bieden wij jou?

Naast de genoemde leuke functie binnen een groeiend en innovatief bedrijf bieden wij:

· Salaris: We bieden je een salaris tussen € 5.590 en € 7.958 per maand (o.b.v. 40 uur per week), afhankelijk van je ervaring en kennis;

· Middelen: Leaseauto, laptop, telefoon;

· Werkdagen: Je bent minimaal 4 dagen per week beschikbaar, al heeft 5 dagen onze voorkeur;

· Vergoeding voor thuiswerken: Je kunt gedeeltelijk thuiswerken en krijgt een onkostenvergoeding van € 2,40 per thuiswerkdag. Ook krijg je een budget van € 750,- om thuis een ergonomische werkplek in te richten;

· Workation: Je kunt tot 30 dagen aaneengesloten per jaar vanuit het buitenland werken;

· Leuke teamactiviteiten: Leer je collega’s beter kennen door deel te nemen aan maandelijkse evenementen georganiseerd door ons energieke Fun-team, zoals een pubquiz, Zomer BBQ, wine & beer tastings en movie night;

· Vakantiedagen: Je krijgt 25 vakantiedagen en de mogelijkheid om maximaal 20 extra dagen bij te kopen;

· Groei en ontwikkeling: De mogelijkheid om je vaardigheden en verantwoordelijkheden te ontwikkelen binnen de functie, middels opleidingen en Linkedin learning, of door te stromen naar een van de andere functies binnen CCS;

· Vakantiegeld: Jaarlijks 8,33%;

· Voordelen: Je krijgt een aantrekkelijke pensioenregeling met een lage eigen bijdrage en kunt gebruikmaken van collectieve verzekeringen met korting. Ook is er een bedrijfsfitnessregeling voor een gezonde levensstijl en een fietsregeling voor duurzaam vervoer.

Waarom CCS?

Omdat wij geloven dat werk meer is dan een baan. Het is een plek waar je jezelf kunt zijn, impact kunt maken en kunt groeien. Het is een omgeving waar je wordt geïnspireerd om het beste uit jezelf te halen en samen te werken aan een duurzame toekomst. Kom bij ons en ontdek wat er mogelijk is als je een carrière bouwt vol passie, plezier en betekenis. Jij bent de ontbrekende schakel in ons team. Word onderdeel van ons verhaal. 🚀

title: (Senior) Recruiter - Growing Impact Scale Up
description:
Join us in Revolutionizing Supply Chains
We’re a fast-growing SaaS scale-up on a mission to shape a sustainable future for the food industry. With four years of continuous 100% year-on-year growth, our team is expanding quickly. We’re looking for a proactive, highly organised Recruiter to help us find the people who will drive that growth, and to help shape how we work as we scale. Join us and shape the future of food sustainability with us!

About Simvia

Ensuring responsible supply chains is one of the largest challenges of our time. At Simvia we are on a path to enable the food and consumer goods industry to become a force for good, by making it simple to prove that what we eat and use is safe, compliant, and sustainable. 

Several of Europe's largest retailers, from Albert Heijn to Edeka, have joined Simvia together with their suppliers, and our network now spans more than 200,000 suppliers in 130 countries. AI gives us a strong tailwind: our network holds unique data, and much of the manual work in compliance can now be automated. We are growing rapidly and keep scaling with a driven, international team of 75+ people in the heart of Amsterdam. 

About this role

You will be our first in-house Recruiter. There is no recruitment playbook yet, so you build it: the process, the guardrails and the habits that let us hire fast and well as we scale. That calls for someone who thinks "I'll find a way" rather than "what's the rule here?" 

Sourcing is the heart of the job. Most of your impact comes from finding and convincing great people who were not looking. Every person you bring in shapes the company we become, so we want someone who lives our culture, not only someone who can describe it. 

Who thrives here

Our culture is driven and kind, and it only works if you bring both. 

Driven by the mission. You set ambitious goals, own the outcome, and welcome a high bar. 

Frank. You say what you think and would rather hear the truth than a comfortable story. 

Open. You ask for feedback and change your mind when the facts change. 

Trusting. You build real relationships and give others room to own their work. 

If this sounds more draining than energizing, that is a useful signal too. 

What you will work on

  • Sourcing and approaching great people across sales, customer success, product and engineering, through LinkedIn, referrals and cold calls, so most of our hires come from you rather than agencies 

  • Building our recruitment process from scratch: clear steps, interview templates and scorecards that every hiring manager follows 

  • Running several hiring processes at once, from role profile to signed offer, with candidates always knowing where they stand 

  • Holding hiring managers, senior leaders included, to agreed timelines and fast feedback 

  • Tracking time to hire, source effectiveness and funnel conversion, and using the numbers to improve how we hire 

  • Helping our People & Culture team with in-house events and office life in quieter hiring periods 

What you bring

  • 3+ years as a recruiter, in-house or agency, with hires across SaaS or tech roles from sales to R&D 

  • Real sourcing strength: direct approach and cold calls give you energy, and you can point to hires you found yourself 

  • A builder's mindset: you enjoy setting up processes, templates and guardrails where none exist yet 

  • Highly organized: you run many roles and steps at once without dropping anything 

  • You enjoy speed, and you are assertive with senior stakeholders while staying warm with candidates 

  • You already use AI and automation in your work and are curious about the next tool

  • Fluent English, written and spoken 

Nice to have

  • German and/or Dutch, German being the most useful 

  • Experience in a start-up or scale-up 

  • Experience with an ATS and LinkedIn Recruiter 

What we offer

  • A high-paced organization with room to grow your career 

  • A meaningful mission: help the food and consumer goods industry become a force for good 

  • Training and support, a pension contribution and travel reimbursement 

  • Fresh lunch every day, monthly Thirsty Thursdays, hackathons, boat parties and our annual dance event 

  • At least three days per week in our Amsterdam city center office, with two rooftop terraces 

How we hire

An intro call with our People & Culture team, a conversation with the hiring manager, an assignment, a culture conversation and an offer. Every process includes an assignment, because we would rather see your work than hear about it. We move fast and keep you informed at every step.

We hire people with different backgrounds, cultures, and views because it makes our work better. Whoever you are, wherever you are from, whoever you love and whatever you believe in, you are welcome here.

description:
Help fix customer-centricity at scale


Every company wants to become more customer-centric. At TheyDo, we make that ambition real. Our AI-powered journey management platform helps the world’s largest enterprises align around what matters most: their customers. By bringing scattered data and teams together, we empower smarter decisions and better experiences. Since 2019, global leaders across industries — including Ford, Cisco, Johnson & Johnson, Siemens, Home Depot, and Lufthansa — have trusted us to scale journey management and deliver measurable impact.

Backed by $50M from top-tier investors, including Blossom and 20VC, we are building a category-defining company. Our fully remote team of 100+ TheyDoers represents 30+ nationalities across 27 countries, united by a customer-led, people-first culture.

Our mission is clear: Make journey management the most powerful business tool in the world.

If you’re looking for a place where your work shapes the future of how companies operate, join us. Let’s build it together.

The role

Journey management is becoming a must-have for the world's biggest companies, and TheyDo is the platform leading the category. Enterprises like Ford, Cisco, Vodafone and Pfizer already use TheyDo to understand their customers end to end and decide where to act.

Now we're going after the rest of Europes biggest brands, and we want you leading the charge. As a Senior Account Executive, you'll take a greenfield territory of enterprise accounts, open the doors, and land the new logos that define TheyDo's next chapter.

You'll be based in the Benelux, working remotely and reporting to Stephan. You'll join a team of 6 EU AEs, backed by SDR, Enablement and Customer Success colleagues across North America and Europe.

Why this role, now

The timing couldn't be better. Customer experience has moved into the boardroom, and enterprises want a way to turn it into decisions. TheyDo gives them that, and our customers are proving it.

Europe is wide open. Your target list is full of companies that look just like the ones already buying from us, and most of them have never had a TheyDo conversation. We know what wins. Now we need someone to scale it and put their name on the logos that come next.

This is the moment to join: early enough to shape how we win, with the proof that we do.

What you'll do

This is a role built around creating revenue that didn't exist before, not managing revenue that already does.

Build your own pipeline. You'll start from a target list, not a book.

  • Own a named list of Benelux enterprise accounts and decide where to focus, based on signal rather than hope

  • Source most of your pipeline yourself through outbound, account-based plays with BDR and Marketing, events and executive networking

  • Break into accounts with no existing relationship and find the senior person who owns the customer experience problem


Win the first deal. You'll take a cold account all the way to signature.

  • Run complex, multi-stakeholder cycles from first conversation through discovery, business case, procurement and close

  • Sell on value to C-level and VP buyers across CX, Product and Digital: a business case a CFO will sign, not a feature tour

  • Land mid-to-high six-figure first deals, structured to expand, and hand them to Customer Success with the context to grow them

Shape how we win. You'll help write the European playbook.

  • Refine our ICP, messaging and sales motion based on what you see in the field

  • Share buyer insight with Product so they can act on it

  • Forecast accurately and keep the team informed through clear async updates

What this role isn't

We'd rather be clear now than have the wrong person find out six months in.

  • It isn't account management. You won't inherit renewals or an installed base to upsell. If most of your number has come from growing existing customers, this probably isn't your role.

  • It isn't inbound-led. Marketing and SDR will support you, but you'll be expected to create most of your own pipeline.

  • It isn't a finished machine. If you need fully built enablement, years of territory data and a playbook that tells you what to do next, you'll find this frustrating. If you want to help build those things, you'll find it energizing.

What we're looking for

  • 4+ years closing B2B SaaS deals, with most of that in enterprise new-business roles selling into enterprise organizations.

  • A track record of exceeding annual quotas, where the majority of your closed revenue came from net-new logos you sourced yourself. Be ready to walk us through the numbers.

  • Proven ability to land mid-to-high six-figure first deals with enterprises that weren't customers before.

  • Experience selling a platform or new-category product, where you had to create the need rather than respond to an RFP.

  • A value-selling methodology (MEDDPICC, Command of the Message or similar) you actually use, not just know.

  • Confidence engaging C-level buyers, building consensus across stakeholders and navigating enterprise procurement, security and legal

  • You'd rather start with a blank target list than a handed-over book, and you're energized by a scale-up where the product and playbook move fast

Bonus points if you have experience selling to CX, Product, Digital or Design leaders
